Individuals with CF have an increased incidence of osteopenia
and osteoporosis, and an increased risk of fractures. Contribut-
ing factors include deﬁ ciencies of vitamin D, vitamin K, and 
calcium; use of corticosteroids; disease severity; inactivity and 
low body mass; hypogonadism; and malnutrition.146 Children
age 8 and older who have risk factors for bone disease should 
have their bone mass evaluated using dual-energy X-ray 
absorptiometry (DXA). Additionally, children at risk for poor
bone health should have serum calcium, phosphorus, parathy-
roid hormone, and 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels measured.
Table 21.7 outlines the timeline for nutrition assessment, in-
